name: Cozy Artist’s Abode! NE Minneapolis, Pets, Wifi
description:
**Please send a message of inquiry (scroll down to "contact host") before requesting dates. So appreciated!

Make my home your homebase while you check out all Mpls offers. My home is in a prime part of NE Mpls! Home to artists, lots of new craft breweries & pub crawls, ethnic eating strip, retro shops, cafes, live music, parks ! Location Location! Quick drive to downtown, U of M, and all the major freeways, very centrally located. A comfortable place to lay your head between activities.
neighborhood_overview:
The area:
Welcome to NE Minneapolis! Coming to town to tour our incredible NE Minneapolis breweries? Or for theater, farmers markets, or our great local Arts events? A business convention? Or to visit nearby relatives? NE Minneapolis is a convenient, centrally located, yet safe, residential spot for your homebase. It's artsy, quaint, and full of neighborhood bars and restaurants, many of them with acclaimed chefs and locally raised ingredients! Pub crawls are very popular in NE because it's so easy to walk from one bar to the next, and each has its own individual flavor. :) My house happens to be just over a century old, though you wouldn't know it from looking at it, it does retain some of that great old character.

The neighborhood is all residential with sidewalks, though a short, 1.5 block walk to restaurants and major grocery store, Target, etc. There is a large park with wading pool, tennis courts, soccer/ice skating just one block from the house. Freeway
host_about:
Hi, I'm Emily! I’ve been hosting on Airbnb since 2008, when it began! I have worked to make my home a comfortable place for guests and appreciate the great interactions and friendships I have made. My house is colorful, eclectic, retro/boho. It’s a cheerful place and I love to use color and artwork to express happy feelings. I love to paint, cook and garden - hopefully you get a chance to enjoy the back garden! 

I live in the Arts District of NE Minneapolis, a quaint area of Minneapolis. The Windom park neighborhood of “Nordeast” is a quiet, residential neighborhood with sidewalks. Nearby there are lots of things to keep you busy; a park with wading pool, a water park with miniature golf, tennis courts, bike and walking paths. Just 2 blocks away are; Target, Cub Foods grocery store, gift shops, coffee shops, and many others for everything you may need. 

In the house you will find a welcome book with a list of many nearby restaurants within walking distance, lots of breweries, sights to see and other details on the house. I hope to host you comfortably during your stay in Minneapolis!

The curving, hilly and shady streets are a great place for a walk. Architecture ranges from big old Victorian painted ladies, Frank Lloyd Wright's very first 1934 prairie school Usonian  home to contemporary glass houses designed by famous architects and small bungalows. Emma’s Spectacle Lake Home is located on the clear and beautiful 239 square acre Spectacle Lake, eight miles west of Cambridge, Minnesota.

Longing for a North Woods retreat but don’t want to spend precious vacation hours on the highway? Emma’s Spectacle Lake Home is the place for you. Travel just one hour north of the Twin Cities to historic Isanti County where the wild and scenic Rum River runs for 153 miles, old growth stands of White Pine dot the landscape, pristine lakes and unspoiled wetlands thrive, and abundant and varied wildlife are plentiful. All of this combines to provide the classic North Woods experience.
Whether you are looking for a quiet couple’s getaway or an activity-packed family holiday, Emma’s Spectacle Lake Home offers many varied opportunities for enjoyment and relaxation.

David D Peterson, the owner’s grandfather,grew up in the County. Enchanted by the bounty and magnificence the area had to offer, David   D  bought property on Spectacle Lake. One of David’s sons and the owner’s father, Don H Peterson, married his wife, Emma, in the early 1940s. David D and his wife had 7 children 2 girls and 5 sons. All 5 boys fought in World War II and, luckily, all 5 survived. Upon their return the boys began to purchase property on Spectacle Lake. Captivated by the Lake and wanting to continue the family tradition, Emma secretly saved her money and bought an adjacent lot for her family. As the next generation grew, they too bought lots and, in due course, built their own homes. This was the origin of Emma’s Spectacle Lake Home. Spectacle Lake is full of this kind of history. These are not transient vacation homes. The neighborhood is established and quiet. This is the perfect location for anyone who wants a peaceful and undisturbed getaway.

Single-family charm with big building amenities.

Enjoy the hundreds of miles of bike trails, sail on Lake Bde Maka Ska, take the historic trolley just steps away to an outdoor summer concert on Lake Harriet or just enjoy a casual laid-back week/weekend hanging out in one of the coolest cities in the USA. Locals, including our beloved Prince, have considered Minneapolis one of the best cities in America and a well-kept secret for years.

An animal lover and advocate and  I have Moki a rescue dog. I've traveled the world and always love coming back to my beautiful City of Lakes.

host_about:
Welcome!  I'm your host along with my busy sometimes loud family! I've had fun adventures with AirBnB and have enjoyed hosting for more than 10 years. I love my historic 1800s home as much as I love to travel and meet new people. And I'm looking forward to having you as a guest! I live, work, play and volunteer in the community here in the W7th neighborhood known as Little Bohemia. I really enjoy this unique historic part of St. Paul—it feels like a small town but it's right in the city.

I'm always up for recommending walking/hiking routes, local parks and/or dog parks, local shopping places, and the best locally owned dining. From beautiful historic oak groves, like Irvine Park, to sprawling interconnected wildlife corridors, like Crosby Farm to Hidden Falls and Fort Snelling State Park, and scenic sunsets you might just forget you're in a city.

We have lots of outdoor rec opportunities here in St Paul, from mountain biking, snowshoeing, and ice skating to year-round hiking. There is free music, dancing, yoga and more in the parks throughout summer (and some really cool secret neighborhood music nights that I can tell you about, just ask me!). Check out the Bluff to Bluff Urban Hike I host via AirBnB Experiences!

West 7th, the West End, has many antique and boutique local shops, wonderful local historic restaurants, breakfast places and great coffee shops - several within walking distance from my home. Of course, the Mall of America is only 15 minutes away. Downtown is 5 minutes. And several more chain and local shops are just a 5-minute jaunt up the hill on Grand Ave. 

Several hospitals blocks from house, incl Children's and United.

No matter why you are in St Paul, you'll find a way to connect with something special! Let me help you to discover and love St Paul, Minnesota.

Ask about sleds, bicycles, firewood, charcoal, etc. I'm happy to let you use these.

name: Cozy with that Special Feeling
description: Charming, cozy house close to the St. Paul campus of the University of Minnesota--pass through farm fields daily, while still in the city.  Bus 5 or walk 17 minutes to the UMN St. Paul campus or bus either downtown Minneapolis or to the UMN main campus. Enjoy backyard and screen porch retreats.  This is 1 of 2 cozy bedrooms upstairs for guests. Kitchen & laundry, too! Plus bedding and towels. Please note the 28 day minimum stay. Covid-19 vaccination preferred.
neighborhood_overview: We live in a neighborhood 3/4 mile from the St. Paul Campus of the University of Minnesota, on a walking and biking route for many students and university staff. Friendly neighborhood with gardens and mature trees. Walk one block to bus line to both downtowns, campus and greenline lightrail.
host_about:
I love running, cross-country skiing, and canoeing, my three fabulous adult children, amazing friends, the north woods and north shore of Minnesota, books and writing.  But there's more!--Colombia and Ecuador are dear to my heart, yet one of my favorite places on earth is my hammock on my back back porch.  I pretty much live out there all summer--as if it were a cabin, accessible by passing through a door.  Magic!  I eat my oatmeal out there every morning in the summer, and read (with the birds.)

I lived in Colombia for a year when I was fifteen, and the hospitality and ardor of my Colombian friends changed me forever. If I could I would travel up and down the spine of the Andes by bus, taking in the mountains, the people, the food, the music and passion.  Being open and welcoming is what I wish to offer my guests, too.  I love connections, people and living fully.  I also have Scandinavian roots, and here in Minnesota we generalize that this gives us a bit too much reserve.  This is why I say "Colombia saved me" at a tender age.  Nevertheless, I also honor my guests' independence and need for privacy and autonomy. 

I do have a secret life motto:  live poetically.  How cheesy--but it's so good!

I've worked as a wilderness guide and in the hospitality industry for the past 5 decades. With roller skating, canoe camping, backpacking, downhill skiing, kayaking, fly fishing, rock climbing and mountain biking keeping me occupied I never did have time to look for a corporate cubicle!

•1 block south you’ll find Selby Avenue, with its one-of-a-kind restaurants, bars, cafes, and boutiques.

•0.4 mile south will have you on breathtaking Summit Avenue, hailed as the nation’s best preserved stretch of Victorian-era mansions and the perfect place for a leisurely self-guided stroll or to take part in one of the many expert-led historic walking tours (don’t miss the famous F. Scott Fitzgerald Rowhouse and Sinclair Lewis mansion!).

description:
We can’t wait to host you in our bright+spacious+charming+no smoking guesthouse, your ideal home-away-from-home base to explore + enjoy all the Twin Cities has to offer!

Nestled in the heart of Seward, we’re close to MSP airport+Downtown Mpls+Mississippi River+ U of MN + St. Paul as well Abbot Northwestern Hospital, M Health Fairview Hospital, Children's Hospital + Hennepin County Medical Center.

Added bonus; we are right next door to Darling, a family friendly, delicious neighborhood cafe!
neighborhood_overview:
Seward is a diverse, vibrant neighborhood located along the Mississippi River in south Minneapolis, close to downtown, the University, and Saint Paul. Seward's sense of community and mix of residential, commercial, and industrial areas give the neighborhood the feel of an urban village within a large metropolitan area. Our corner of Seward is home to Big River Yoga Studio, Common Ground Meditation Center, Cafe Racer, Curry in a Hurry, Seward Co-op, all within one mile.
Walk out the back door, head east and within 5 minutes you'll be at the beautiful Mississippi River Gorge with walking, hiking and trail running paths and lots of nature to enjoy. Look up! Why yes those are eagles! There are also two wonderful play parks both with kiddie pools, an awesome bookstore (Boneshaker Books) and a fantastic gift shop (Corazon) all within a 3/4 mile radius. We LOVE our 'hood!
host_about:
We are a casual, bustling family-friendly cafe nestled in the heart of the Seward neighborhood of Minneapolis.  An established leader in the Twin Cities local food movement, we've been cooking up and serving Good Real Food® and cultivating community for over 22 years.  Recently named best Eco Friendly/Farm to Table restaurant in Minnesota by Travel & Leisure Magazine, we source with pride and intention taking care that the land, the animals and the people we work with are treated with LOVE and respect.  You can taste the difference! At Birchwood, people come from all over to feel right at home and we're excited to extend our hospitality next door to the Birchwood Guest House.  Food connects us All and All are Welcome here. 

At Birchwood Cafe we believe that Black Lives Matter, Women's Rights are Human Rights, No human is illegal, Science is Real, Love is Love & Kindness is Everything. 

The Birchwood Guest House is the former home of cafe owner Tracy Singleton. 
 A mom, dog lover, yogi, cycling enthusiast, Harry Potter fan, connector, community builder and advocate for a fair food system for all, Tracy still lives very close by with her daughter Lily and doodle Vigo.

​Southeast of the central business district, the South Ninth Street area served as an important zone of transition between the downtown commercial core and outlying lower density residential districts. The area remains unique for being the only neighborhood in Minneapolis with a linkage of serial housing, featuring prominent local architects.

name: Deluxe Queen at Erik's Retreat
description:
Erik’s Retreat is a nonprofit organization that offers upscale guest accommodations run by young adults with autism. They are concierges, chefs, tour guides, and more! Meaningful careers are scarce for them.

You're part of the solution.

When you stay with us, you’ll be centrally located with wonderful amenities, all while providing living quarters, social opportunities, and significant work for our members.

Welcome to Erik's Retreat. Where vision knows no bounds.

Please visit our website!
neighborhood_overview: Erik’s Retreat is located in the center of everything the Twin Cities has to offer. We are a ten-minute drive from the Mall of America and downtown Minneapolis. We are also within walking or biking distance to Lake Harriet and a number of parks and lakes. The Southdale Center shopping mall is in our backyard and high-end shopping is available just minutes away at Galleria. Additionally, we are very close to the Bloomington, Edina, and Eden Prairie business corridor off of I-494.
host_about:
Founder and CEO, Erik's Ranch, Inc.
Kathryn Nordberg has held executive positions with organizations in technology, packaged goods and health care. She is recognized for innovative solutions to long-standing operational challenges and her ability to create positive outcomes for long-term projects with multimillion-dollar budgets. She has leadership experience in strategic and organizational planning, management, marketing, partnership development and alliances, sales, new product development and communications.

Nordberg also has an adult son with autism. She became the founding chairperson of Families for Early Autism Treatment in 1995 when no funding or early intervention programs were available in Minnesota. In 1997, she participated in bringing behavioral therapist Ivar Lovaas to Minnesota to share his Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) for early intervention with children with autism. The South Ninth Street Historic District exhibits one of the city’s best and most cohesive collections of multiple-family dwellings from the turn of the century. Generally located along Ninth and 10th streets between the intersections of Park Avenue and Fifth Avenue

During the mid-1880s, the young City of Minneapolis was booming. The flour milling industry had hit full stride, bringing thousands of hopeful newcomers to town in search of new jobs and new homes. A rapid influx of new residents between 1880 and 1890 created a severe shortage of housing. As architects and builders scrambled to meet the demands, a new type of building – the row house – was introduced to the Minneapolis streetscape.


The first residents to settle in the South Ninth Street District were affluent professionals drawn to the area by its proximity to the downtown business district. Many of these wealthy businessmen, such as Samuel Morse, vice president of the Minneapolis Flour and Manuf

host_about:
Founder and CEO, Erik's Ranch, Inc.
Kathryn Nordberg has held executive positions with organizations in technology, packaged goods and health care. She is recognized for innovative solutions to long-standing operational challenges and her ability to create positive outcomes for long-term projects with multimillion-dollar budgets. She has leadership experience in strategic and organizational planning, management, marketing, partnership development and alliances, sales, new product development and communications.

Nordberg also has an adult son with autism. She became the founding chairperson of Families for Early Autism Treatment in 1995 when no funding or early intervention programs were available in Minnesota. In 1997, she participated in bringing behavioral therapist Ivar Lovaas to Minnesota to share his Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) for early intervention with children with autism. She also challenged the Minneapolis public school system status quo, creating awareness about the lack of efficacy of its program for children with autism, laying the groundwork for the assistance available for families desiring ABA.

With Nordberg’s experience as the foundation for Erik’s Retreat, we understand the need for individual choices and how to support that. Through professionally trained staff, careful planning and communication with residents, members, and families, and the employment of innovation in everything we do, we believe that living a life of promise is within everyone’s reach. “I believe that if I can imagine it, we can achieve it.”

neighborhood_overview:
The West Seventh neighborhood is one of the oldest in Saint Paul. The neighborhood follows along West Seventh Street and is bound on the north by I-35E or the River Bluffs and by the Mississippi River to the South. It formed in the late 1830s from discharged soldiers and other pioneers building houses along the Mississippi River. Later, a boat dock south of Fort Snelling known as the Upper Landing became an important landing spot for dropping off settlers and supplies. The neighborhood grew as waves of settlers and immigrant came to the area to farm or work for local industrial sites. A sizable amount of industry is located between the Mississippi River and south of West Seventh Street. Workers built their houses close to local industry and different ethnic enclaves developed with the different waves of immigrants.

City of Saint Paul is home to United Hospital, Children's Hospital, Regions Hospital, HealthEast, and others.

neighborhood_overview:
The 9th St Historic District is located in Elliot Park, which is central Minneapolis that includes the US Bank Stadium.

The South Ninth Street Historic District exhibits one of the city’s best and most cohesive collections of multiple-family dwellings from the turn of the century. Generally located along Ninth and 10th streets between the intersections of Park Avenue and Fifth Avenue, the district also extends south to include properties along East 14th and East 16th streets.

Southeast of the central business district, the South Ninth Street area served as an important zone of transition between the downtown commercial core and outlying lower density residential districts. The area remains unique for being the only neighborhood in Minneapolis with a linkage of serial housing, featuring prominent local architects.During the mid-1880s, the young City of Minneapolis was booming. The flour milling industry had hit full stride, bringing thousands of hopeful newcomers

This place will feel like your home away from home whether you are sipping wine by the fireplace, curled up with a good book in the reading nook, gazing at stars through the skylights in the upper loft, or laughing with friends in the open kitchen. If you are in town for a business trip or a romantic getaway to the city, we are conveniently located in a quiet neighborhood close to all Minneapolis has to offer!
neighborhood_overview:
The Modern Refuge is located in the Standish neighborhood, which is safe and quiet. It really is a prime location; it is a 10-15 minute drive to the airport, Mall of America, uptown, NE Minneapolis, and downtown.

Some of our favorite local establishments near by are Northbound Smokehouse and Brewpub where you can find local craft beers and a tasty meal to go with it, Sister Sludge is just around the corner and is a local favorite for coffee and wine, the Standish Cafe is a small neighborhood cafe, and A Baker's Wife Pastry Shop is about a 15 minute walk down the road. For those that love to golf, Hiawatha Golf Course is only two miles away. And for those who want to watch the sunset over Lake Hiawatha you can walk there in about 20 minutes, or keep walking south and you will run into Lake Nokomis to go for a run, walk, bike ride, picnic, hammocking, or rent a kayak/canoe.
host_about: Hi, I'm Heather! I am originally from northern Minnesota, but have fallen in love with Minneapolis. My husband (Ryan, also a MN native) and I truly want you to feel welcomed and comfortable. We enjoy hosting people and helping others to create memorable experiences we hope you will look back on for years to come.

As architects and builders scrambled to meet the demands, a new type of building – the row house – was introduced to the Minneapolis streetscape.

name: King Room in Boutique Hotel
description:
Custom artwork and a reading nook make this cozy room the right choice for city explorers and business travelers.
Rest up in a king-size bed with luxurious 300-thread-count linens and Simmons Beautyrest® mattress, bathroom with a walk-in rain shower, Frette bathrobe, 55-inch HDTV with premium cable, fully-stocked minibar. host_about:
On the corner of 9th and Hennepin in the heart of Minneapolis’s historic theater district, The Chambers Hotel takes center stage.

Built in 1908, The Chambers has had a front-row seat to the legendary Orpheum Theatre’s groundbreaking performances, from the Marx Brothers’ vaudeville act to Prince’s hometown debut. Click through a few photos from our scrapbook below.

Here at The Chambers, we, too, have a famous flair for the dramatic. Our 60 art-infused guestrooms and suites have walk-in rain showers, deep soaking tubs and sweeping views of vibrant downtown.

A lush courtyard with a fire pit is a prime spot to admire the scenery on Hennepin Avenue. And 12,500 square feet of event space — including a pristine, blank-canvas gallery — await your creative touches.

The skyway just steps from our door leads to the Target Center, Target Field, U.S. Bank Stadium, the Mississippi River and the colorful culture of the Twin Cities. Bravo!

 I offer FREE Keurig coffee and snacks.   My friends would describe me as friendly, open minded, genuine, nice and caring!

For a unique experience, you can try axe throwing, create art at local studios, or enjoy outdoor activities like boating, fishing, and golfing.

Whether you’re into history, outdoor adventures, or just soaking in the scenic beauty, Stillwater and the surrounding St. Croix River Valley have something for everyone!

neighborhood_overview:
Uptown is quite possibly one of the most urban areas in the entire great state of Minnesota. By definition, it functions almost as its own mini-city, and is certainly one of the liveliest communities in the Twin Cities metropolitan area.

Lake Harriet, Lake of the Isles, and Cedar Lake are only a few blocks away, making Uptown’s tree-lined streets both welcoming and walkable— where the blues meet the greens. One of our more recently purchased homes is also close to downtown Sioux Falls and is a two bedroom, so has more space and sleeps up to 6 pretty easily.  

We swapped out another central Sioux Falls home that had been a monthly rental into an Airbnb as well. This is a 5 bedroom house and is close to Sanford, USF and Augustana.  

The most recent purchase in Fall 2022 was an awesome and unique historic home in Balaton, MN. It had already been set up as an Airbnb and we bought it furnished. It has an old home historic feel and is a great and cozy 2 bedrroom.  There is a nice small lake in town and Balaton is close to many scenic spots in SW MN like the Laura Ingalls Wilder museum. 

Then finally, we have two listings located in Bloomington, MN. Patrick and I purchased a house there and did some work to ready it for rental. We have focused on longer term rental (1 month+) in this location. It is located right off 494, close to The Mall of America and the MSP airport. There is a larger, 2 bedroom unit on the main floor and a 2nd unit with a separate entrance and 1 bedroom in the basement.  Patrick lives in the Twin Cities and takes care of the hosting duties for these two units in Bloomington.
